C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-20260904.Summary:
Deliver the next bounded M1.3 browser-service slice by introducing replaceable web-search providers behind an engine-neutral Worldline capability.
The primary product of this change is not an omnibox implementation and not a built-in search engine hard-coded into CEF. The primary product is a small `browser.search/0.1` contract whose provider receives already classified search text and resolves it into a safe navigation target. Navigation remains a separate `browser.navigate` capability invocation.
The first proving provider is a generic structured URL-search plugin that can have multiple installations with different provider configuration. Provider discovery and selection reuse the generic Worldline capability provider-selection machinery rather than creating a browser-specific registry in the kernel.
C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-20260904.Problem:
M1.3 now has browser engine primitives, tabs/history, downloads/cookies, request-policy/adblock and DevTools diagnostics, but there is still no product contract for user-selected web search providers.
Hard-coding a search URL into the future omnibox would couple shell policy to one vendor and would bypass Worldline's provider replacement model. Putting search selection in CEF would make the browser engine own product policy it does not need. Letting a search provider navigate directly would also collapse two distinct authorities: disclosure of query text to a selected provider and mutation of browser page state.
Search queries are potentially sensitive user input. A provider boundary therefore needs explicit authority, bounded input/output, deterministic URL construction, safe scheme/origin rules, payload-free generic telemetry and failure isolation. The architecture must also preserve future room for search suggestions, structured search APIs and semantic/workspace retrieval without pretending those are the same capability as basic web-search navigation.

Goals.Goal: Define an additive experimental `browser.search/0.1` capability contract without changing stable Browser Contract v1.0 semantics.
Define a minimal resolve operation that accepts bounded search text and returns one bounded `SearchNavigationTarget` suitable for a later, separately authorized `browser.navigate` call.
Keep omnibox/address classification outside the search provider. The caller decides that input is search text before invoking `browser.search/resolve`.

Implement one ordinary replaceable `worldline-browser-search` provider plugin whose installation configuration uses a structured fixed base URL, one explicit query parameter name and bounded static parameters rather than arbitrary string concatenation.

Prove multiple installations of the same provider definition can represent different search engines and can be selected/replaced through generic capability provider-selection without changing the consumer.
Prove the search provider itself has no browser navigation, page-action, cookie, storage, download or request-policy authority.
Preserve query privacy: raw query text is visible only to the admitted caller/provider path and is not copied into generic metrics, trajectory, panic text or unrelated events by default.
Add a deterministic S3E proving slice and a real Windows CEF integration proving that a resolved loopback target can be navigated only through a separate authorized browser navigation invocation.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL AND EXACT PLAN APPROVAL ARE SEPARATE. THIS DRAFT DOES NOT AUTHORIZE IMPLEMENTATION.

THE CURRENT BASE BRANCH STILL CONTAINS C-BROWSER-REQUEST-POLICY-INTERCEPTION-SCOPE-CORRECTION-20260902 UNDER `.grace/changes/active` EVEN THOUGH LATER DURABLE PROJECTIONS TREAT THE REQUEST-POLICY SLICE AS COMPLETED. THAT LIFECYCLE INCONSISTENCY MUST BE RECONCILED THROUGH NORMAL GRACE PROCEDURE BEFORE THIS CHANGE'S PLAN IS APPROVED OR EXECUTED. THIS DRAFT DOES NOT AUTHORIZE DIRECT CLEANUP OF THE PREDECESSOR BUNDLE.
SEARCH IS AN ORDINARY REPLACEABLE PLUGIN CAPABILITY. NO SEARCH-ENGINE, PROVIDER-NAME, QUERY-TEMPLATE OR OMNIBOX DOMAIN POLICY MAY ENTER `worldline-kernel`.
CEF AND THE BROWSER ENGINE PROVIDER MUST NOT OWN SEARCH PROVIDER SELECTION OR SEARCH-URL POLICY.
`browser.search/resolve` MUST NOT NAVIGATE A PAGE, OPEN A WINDOW, EXECUTE SCRIPT, MUTATE DOM, READ COOKIES/STORAGE, START DOWNLOADS OR OTHERWISE EXERCISE BROWSER MUTATION AUTHORITY.

RESOLVING SEARCH TEXT AND NAVIGATING TO THE RESULT ARE SEPARATE AUTHORIZED CAPABILITY INVOCATIONS. POSSESSION OF SEARCH RESOLUTION AUTHORITY MUST NOT IMPLY `NavigatePage` OR ANY OTHER BROWSER AUTHORITY.
EVENT BUS IS NOT RPC. SEARCH RESOLUTION RETURNS THROUGH THE NORMAL CAPABILITY REQUEST/RESULT PATH; EVENTS MAY OBSERVE BOUNDED METADATA AFTER AN OUTCOME BUT MAY NOT DETERMINE OR REPLACE THE RESULT.

PROVIDER DISCOVERY AND SELECTION MUST REUSE GENERIC CAPABILITY DISCOVERY/SELECTION. DO NOT ADD A SEARCH-SPECIFIC REGISTRY OR SPECIAL PROVIDER-SELECTION PATH TO THE KERNEL. IF THE EXISTING GENERIC MECHANISM CANNOT EXPRESS THE REQUIRED EXPLICIT/DURABLE SELECTION SEMANTICS, STOP AND REPLAN RATHER THAN HIDING SEARCH SELECTION IN CEF OR SHELL CODE.
THE V0.1 PROVING PROVIDER MUST CONSTRUCT TARGET URLS STRUCTURALLY. SEARCH TEXT MUST NOT BE CONCATENATED INTO RAW URL STRINGS, SCHEMES, AUTHORITIES, HOSTNAMES OR PATHS.

PRODUCTION SEARCH TARGET CONFIGURATION MUST USE HTTPS. HTTP IS PERMITTED ONLY FOR DETERMINISTIC LOOPBACK TEST FIXTURES. `javascript:`, `data:`, `file:`, `about:` AND OTHER NON-WEB EXECUTION/LOCAL-RESOURCE SCHEMES ARE OUT OF SCOPE AND MUST BE REJECTED.
SEARCH PROVIDER CONFIGURATION MUST REJECT URL USERINFO/CREDENTIALS, MALFORMED HOSTS, UNBOUNDED STATIC PARAMETERS, EMPTY QUERY-PARAMETER NAMES AND OUTPUTS THAT EXCEED DECLARED SIZE LIMITS.
SEARCH TEXT, STATIC PARAMETER VALUES AND RESULT URLS HAVE FINITE BYTE AND CHARACTER BOUNDS. OVERSIZED INPUT OR OUTPUT FAILS EXPLICITLY WITHOUT PANIC OR PARTIAL NAVIGATION.

SEARCH QUERY TEXT IS POTENTIALLY SENSITIVE. RAW QUERY TEXT MUST NOT ENTER GENERIC METRICS, TRAJECTORY, PANIC TEXT, DEBUG FORMATTING OR UNRELATED EVENTS BY DEFAULT. EXISTING PAYLOAD-FREE INVOCATION AUDIT MAY RECORD OPERATION/PROVIDER/OUTCOME METADATA WITHOUT THE QUERY BODY.

FAILURE, ABSENCE, UNLOAD, QUARANTINE, TIMEOUT OR REPLACEMENT OF A SEARCH PROVIDER MUST DEGRADE SEARCH ONLY. DIRECT URL NAVIGATION, TABS, HISTORY, DOWNLOADS, COOKIES, REQUEST POLICY AND DEVTOOLS MUST REMAIN AVAILABLE.
STABLE Browser Contract v1.0 AND EXISTING EXPERIMENTAL BROWSER-SERVICE, ENGINE, REQUEST-POLICY AND DEVTOOLS CONTRACTS MUST NOT BE INCOMPATIBLY REDEFINED. SEARCH STARTS AS A NEW EXPERIMENTAL CONTRACT.
NO PUBLIC-INTERNET DEPENDENCY IS ALLOWED IN ACCEPTANCE TESTS. REAL CEF EVIDENCE MUST USE LOOPBACK TARGETS WITH STAGED/PINNED CEF RUNTIME.
NON-WINDOWS WORKSPACE COMPILATION MUST REMAIN GREEN. REAL CEF S3E MAY BE WINDOWS-ONLY AND MUST REPORT EXPLICIT Unsupported/Unavailable ELSEWHERE.
GRACE LINT IS A LIFECYCLE PREFLIGHT AND FINAL OUTER GATE; DO NOT NEST `grace lint` INSIDE PRODUCT `MustPassCommand` OR TREAT IT AS RUNTIME ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Remote search suggestions or autocomplete APIs.
Structured SERP result parsing or a search-results API.
Image, news, shopping or other vertical-search contracts.
Workspace semantic retrieval or history search.
Provider-specific authentication or paid search APIs.
Choosing a permanent product default search vendor.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: An experimental `browser.search/0.1` contract exists in the browser service contract layer and contains no CEF, Chromium, HWND, raw pointer, filesystem-path or platform-specific types.
The contract defines one bounded resolve operation with an explicit search authority and a bounded result carrying a navigation target, while navigation remains outside the contract.
The search authority is disjoint from page observation, navigation, actions, cookies, storage, downloads, request-policy and DevTools authorities.
A principal holding only search resolution authority can resolve a target but receives AccessDenied if it attempts browser navigation through the normal browser capability boundary.
`worldline-browser-search` can be installed more than once with distinct structured provider configuration and each installation exposes the same `browser.search/0.1` capability contract.
Generic provider selection can select provider installation A or B and an unchanged consumer receives the corresponding target without provider-name branching in consumer code.
Provider replacement/unload invalidates old runtime authority/handles and a replacement provider does not inherit stale runtime authority.

Search target construction uses a parsed fixed web origin/path, one validated query parameter name and bounded static parameters. Search text is encoded as a query-parameter value using deterministic URL encoding.
Unicode, spaces, reserved characters, percent signs and fragment-looking input cannot escape the query parameter or alter scheme/authority/host.
Production configuration rejects non-HTTPS remote targets, URL userinfo, malformed hosts and forbidden schemes; loopback HTTP is accepted only in explicitly test-scoped configuration.
Oversized queries, static parameters or output URLs fail explicitly and deterministically without panic, allocation growth or browser mutation.
Raw query text is absent from generic metrics, trajectory payloads, panic text and unrelated events in acceptance evidence.
A deterministic S3E fixture proves two configured search providers produce distinct loopback navigation targets for the same input and proves provider selection/replacement without consumer changes.

A hosted/staged Windows real-CEF S3E path uses the normal native provider process and rejects ReferenceBrowserBackend substitution while proving the separately authorized navigation reaches the resolved loopback target.
Search-provider crash/unload/unavailability does not break direct URL navigation or existing M1.3 service proving slices.

Architecture checks prevent search-provider/vendor/configuration domain types from entering worldline-kernel or worldline-browser-cef and prevent worldline-browser-search from becoming a dependency of unrelated browser services.

A dedicated BrowserSearch CI suite or an explicitly separated extension of BrowserServices covers contract bounds, authority separation, provider replacement, privacy, deterministic S3E and staged real-CEF S3E evidence.

Existing Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice, RealChromium, BrowserProvider, BrowserServices, BrowserRequestPolicy, BrowserDevTools, RealS3B and All gates are preserved and not weakened.

Completion evidence distinguishes scaffolded, wired and verified claims, reports local versus hosted evidence separately and does not apply GRACE graph/verification projections until explicit owner apply confirmation.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh evidence names the experimental search contract, the selected provider/runtime topology, authority separation, deterministic URL encoding and bounds, provider replacement, query privacy, zero-origin-hit proof before navigation, separately authorized loopback navigation, real staged CEF provider identity, failure isolation and preserved existing browser-service gates. Local and hosted evidence are reported separately.

Assumptions.Assumption: Generic Worldline capability discovery/provider selection can select among multiple installations that expose the same search capability. The plan must inspect and prove this assumption before introducing any search-specific selection store.
The initial useful browser-search capability only needs to resolve already classified text to a navigation target; remote suggestions and structured search results can be separate later capabilities.

A structured fixed base URL plus one query parameter and bounded static parameters is sufficient for the first proving providers. More exotic path-template providers require a later additive design if real product need appears.
Existing browser navigation and real CEF loopback proving infrastructure can consume a resolved target without requiring a browser-engine search primitive.
Search provider configuration is installation-owned configuration/state and does not need to become part of stable Browser Contract v1.0.
Exact seed provider presets and any eventual default search choice are product/configuration decisions that may follow after the engine-neutral capability is proven.
